title: Power of Four
summary: Determine if an integer is a power of four by checking if there exists an integer x such that the integer equals 4 raised to the power of x.
statement: Determine if an integer is a power of four by checking if there exists an integer x such that the integer equals 4 raised to the power of x.
constraints: -(2^31) <= n <= 2^31-1. Return whether n = 4^x for a nonnegative integer x.
1 is a valid power. A power of two is a power of four only when its set bit has an even zero-based position.
reference_solution:
def is_power_of_four(n):
    return n > 0 and n & (n-1) == 0 and n & 0x55555555 != 0
hints: Powers of four are powers of two with the single set bit in positions 0,2,4,... .
First require n>0 and n&(n-1)==0; then check membership in the alternating-bit mask.
Return n>0 and n&(n-1)==0 and n&0x55555555!=0 for the fixed 32-bit domain.
The mask has ones at exactly the even bit positions. Repeated division by four is another valid approach.
editorial: Clearing the lowest set bit leaves zero exactly for positive powers of two. Intersecting with 0x55555555 then restricts the bit to an even position, corresponding to 2^(2x)=4^x. Positivity excludes zero and signed negatives. The independent oracle checks the full finite set of allowed powers directly.

tests.explanation: 8=2^3 is a power of two, but not a power of four. Return false.
